findings.claim: The factory registerAidlService path creates the manager and callback implementation, imports RadioExternal::make defined in libril-aidl.so, and publishes the declared V1 AIDL instance. The V1-ndk library supplies generated protocol, not the manager.
Generated service version is 1 and hash is 62c86cf5f8f15456f451d2241b4f21b10627e514. No live lookup was performed.

Native clear transaction 1 uses flags 0x10000001 and no cleanup reply; registration transaction 5 uses flags 0x10000000 and reads status plus an int. The service clear delegates and creates a local OK status; generated one-way dispatch discards it.
Current native raw/segmented indication and segmented response proxies are one-way. Indication segments carry message ID, slot, bytes, index and total length, with no producer-instance field.

findings.kind: static observations with limited concurrency inference
findings.claim: Recovered RadioExternal constructor/registration and generated dispatch add no application mutex around delegated registration. Manager client allocation precedes its mutex; list insertion is locked; initial output follows unlock. Actual concurrent stock execution and duplicate-ID behavior remain untested.

findings.kind: bounded closure and direct static-reference observation
findings.claim: Recovered RadioExternal constructor/registration, wrapper setters and destructors retain/release callback references but do not arm the shared death helper. Direct linkToDeath callers are other radio/RilExt wrappers. This is not global negative evidence or immediate client-death cleanup proof.
Both complete native AIDL split loops send consecutive bounded segments and preserve a full final segment at exact multiples; each stops on failed callback submission. No vendor loop was executed.

findings.kind: static control-flow and ARM64 instruction observation
findings.claim: Raw broadcast and numeric-ID indication use the same manager mutex as clear and retain it through the delegated complete callback call. Pointer/list overloads have no internal lock; initial registration output bypasses that lock. Caller-held serialization and full producer closure remain unqualified.

findings.kind: static evidence and explicit unresolved obligation
findings.claim: Client clear/removal, separate pending-request completion and modem reset are distinct. No reset/drain acknowledgement was recovered from the current Binder method inventory; no fence is relaxed.
